tactics.name: Persistence

tactics.name: Defense Evasion

tactics.name: Discovery

tactics.name: Lateral Movement

tactics.name: Collection

tactics.name: Command and Control

tactics.name: Exfiltration

techniques.name: Direct Prompt Injection
techniques.description: Adversaries input adversarial text or structured prompts directly into a Large Language Model (LLM) or AI interface to override system instructions, bypass security guardrails, or coerce the model into executing unauthorized tool calls.

techniques.name: Indirect Prompt Injection
techniques.description: Adversaries embed malicious instructions inside external content (webpages, uploaded PDFs, emails, source code) that an autonomous AI agent or RAG system ingests, causing the LLM to execute unintended commands upon reading.

techniques.name: Query Public AI Services
techniques.description: Adversaries query public AI services (commercial LLMs, generative chatbots) during reconnaissance to synthesize company org charts, draft targeted spearphishing lures, or analyze proprietary source code leaks.

techniques.name: AI Result Poisoning
techniques.description: Adversaries poison training datasets, fine-tuning corpora, or vector database embeddings so the AI model generates corrupted, hallucinatory, or maliciously biased outputs to enterprise users.

techniques.name: Attacks Targeting AI-Assisted Defenses
techniques.description: Adversaries craft adversarial perturbations in malware binaries and network packets specifically engineered to evade machine learning and AI-assisted endpoint detection classifiers.

techniques.name: Abuse of Publish/Subscribe Protocols
techniques.description: Adversaries abuse publish/subscribe messaging protocols (MQTT, DDS, AMQP) on industrial IoT and SCADA networks to publish spoofed control telemetry or subscribe to sensitive field measurement topics.

techniques.name: Industrial DNS Abuse
techniques.description: Adversaries abuse DNS within isolated OT networks by querying rogue DNS resolvers or using DNS tunneling to bridge air-gapped engineering perimeters.

techniques.name: Deliver Malicious Application via Other Means
techniques.description: Adversaries deliver malicious mobile apps outside official app stores using sideloading, alternative third-party marketplaces, or rogue Mobile Device Management (MDM) enrollment profiles.

techniques.name: Active Scanning
techniques.description: Adversaries execute active scanning to gather information about target networks, open ports, and vulnerable services.

techniques.name: Scanning IP Blocks
techniques.description: Adversaries scan entire IPv4/IPv6 blocks belonging to a target organization to map active public hosts.

techniques.name: Vulnerability Scanning
techniques.description: Adversaries scan target systems for known vulnerabilities using automated tools like Nessus or custom scripts.

techniques.name: Gather Victim Network Information
techniques.description: Adversaries harvest victim IP ranges, domain names, DNS records, and network topologies prior to attack.

techniques.name: Phishing for Information
techniques.description: Adversaries send reconnaissance emails to probe corporate defenses and elicit internal employee information.

techniques.name: Acquire Infrastructure
techniques.description: Adversaries buy, lease, or rent infrastructure (domains, VPS servers, CDN accounts) to facilitate operations.

techniques.name: Domains
techniques.description: Adversaries register domains that mimic legitimate brands or companies (typosquatting) for phishing and C2.

techniques.name: Compromise Accounts
techniques.description: Adversaries compromise accounts on third-party services like GitHub, AWS, or email providers to use in attacks.

techniques.name: Obtain Capabilities
techniques.description: Adversaries buy or download malware, exploits, or digital certificates on dark web forums.

techniques.name: Phishing
techniques.description: Adversaries send phishing messages to gain initial access, tricking users into running malware or giving credentials.

techniques.name: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.description: Adversaries attach weaponized documents (macro-enabled Office files, ISOs, ZIPs) to emails.

techniques.name: Spearphishing Link
techniques.description: Adversaries include malicious hyperlinks leading to credential harvesting pages or drive-by downloads.

techniques.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
techniques.description: Adversaries exploit vulnerabilities in internet-accessible software (VPN gateways, web servers, RDP) to gain a foothold.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.description: Adversaries steal or purchase legitimate credentials to log into enterprise systems and services undetected.

techniques.name: Cloud Accounts
techniques.description: Adversaries compromise cloud administrator or service accounts to control cloud workloads.

techniques.name: External Remote Services
techniques.description: Adversaries leverage external-facing remote services like VPNs, Citrix, and Remote Desktop to enter networks.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
techniques.description: Adversaries abuse command and script interpreters to execute arbitrary commands, scripts, and binaries.

techniques.name: PowerShell
techniques.description: Adversaries execute malicious commands via PowerShell, often using encoded or obfuscated syntax.

techniques.name: Windows Command Shell
techniques.description: Adversaries abuse cmd.exe to launch commands, manage files, and invoke batch scripts.

techniques.name: Unix Shell
techniques.description: Adversaries abuse Unix shells (sh, bash, zsh) to run command-line utilities and shell scripts.

techniques.name: User Execution
techniques.description: Adversaries rely on user action to execute malicious payloads, such as opening an email attachment or clicking a link.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Client Execution
techniques.description: Adversaries exploit software vulnerabilities in client applications (browsers, PDF readers, Office apps) to run code.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task/Job
techniques.description: Adversaries abuse task scheduling utilities (cron, Windows Task Scheduler) to facilitate periodic or persistent execution.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task
techniques.description: Adversaries register tasks using schtasks.exe or the Task Scheduler API for persistence.

techniques.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution
techniques.description: Adversaries configure system settings to automatically execute a program upon system boot or user logon.

techniques.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
techniques.description: Adversaries add malicious entries under HKCU/HKLM Run keys or drop shortcuts into the user Startup folder.

techniques.name: Create or Modify System Process
techniques.description: Adversaries create or modify system-level services or daemons to execute malicious binaries on boot.

techniques.name: Windows Service
techniques.description: Adversaries install malicious Windows services with sc.exe or PowerShell to run binaries as SYSTEM.

techniques.name: Access Token Manipulation
techniques.description: Adversaries modify access tokens to operate under a different security context, escalate privileges, or evade detection.

techniques.name: Token Impersonation/Theft
techniques.description: Adversaries duplicate or steal existing access tokens from running privileged processes like LSASS to impersonate logged-in admins.

techniques.name: Create Process with Token
techniques.description: Adversaries create new processes using stolen access tokens to execute binaries under high privilege accounts.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
techniques.description: Adversaries exploit operating system kernel or driver vulnerabilities to elevate rights from standard user to SYSTEM/root.

techniques.name: Process Injection
techniques.description: Adversaries inject code into legitimate processes to evade defenses and inherit elevated access rights.

techniques.name: Dynamic-link Library Injection
techniques.description: Adversaries inject dynamic-link libraries into running processes via CreateRemoteThread and VirtualAllocEx.

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
techniques.description: Adversaries encrypt, encode, or obfuscate contents of executable payloads and scripts to make them difficult to discover.

techniques.name: Indicator Removal
dataSources: Windows Event Log: Event Log Cleared
techniques.description: Adversaries delete or modify generated artifacts (event logs, bash history, temporary files) to hide intrusion tracks.

techniques.name: Clear Windows Event Logs
dataSources: Windows Event Log: Event Log Cleared
techniques.description: Adversaries use wevtutil.exe or PowerShell to clear Security and System event logs.

techniques.name: File Deletion
techniques.description: Adversaries remove malware binaries, scripts, and temporary staging files from disk upon completing actions.

techniques.name: Masquerading
techniques.description: Adversaries manipulate features of their artifacts (filenames, directories, metadata) to disguise them as legitimate utilities.

techniques.name: Hide Artifacts
techniques.description: Adversaries hide files and processes using hidden file attributes, alternate data streams (ADS), or rootkits.

techniques.name: Impair Defenses
techniques.description: Adversaries maliciously modify, disable, or tamper with security tools, firewalls, and logging agents.

techniques.name: Disable or Modify Tools
techniques.description: Adversaries disable or terminate EDR agents, antivirus real-time scanning, and host intrusion prevention systems.

techniques.name: Disable or Modify System Firewall
techniques.description: Adversaries alter firewall rules using netsh or iptables to permit incoming malicious network connections.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping
techniques.description: Adversaries dump plaintext passwords, NTLM hashes, and Kerberos tickets from memory or SAM/NTDS databases.

techniques.name: LSASS Memory
techniques.description: Adversaries dump the memory of the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (lsass.exe) using tools like Mimikatz or procdump.

techniques.name: Brute Force
techniques.description: Adversaries attempt password guessing or password spraying against employee accounts across domain or cloud logins.

techniques.name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets
techniques.description: Adversaries abuse Kerberos protocol weaknesses to perform Kerberoasting, AS-REP roasting, or forge Golden Tickets.

techniques.name: Account Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries query system and domain accounts using net user or LDAP commands to identify high-privilege targets.

techniques.name: System Information Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries harvest operating system version, patch level, and architecture using systeminfo or uname.

techniques.name: Remote System Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries scan or query Active Directory to discover domain controllers, file servers, and databases on the LAN.

techniques.name: Remote Services
techniques.description: Adversaries log into remote systems using valid credentials across administrative protocols.

techniques.name: Remote Desktop Protocol
techniques.description: Adversaries connect to remote servers over port 3389 using RDP clients to control desktop sessions directly.

techniques.name: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
techniques.description: Adversaries copy files and execute commands remotely via hidden administrative shares (C$, ADMIN$).

techniques.name: Lateral Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Adversaries transfer malware or reconnaissance utilities between compromised internal systems over local network shares.

techniques.name: Archive Collected Data
techniques.description: Adversaries compress and encrypt gathered files into ZIP, 7z, or RAR archives prior to exfiltration.

techniques.name: Data from Local System
techniques.description: Adversaries search local hard drives and mounted volumes for intellectual property, source code, and credentials.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol
techniques.description: Adversaries communicate with external C2 servers using standard application protocols (HTTP, HTTPS, DNS) to blend with normal traffic.

techniques.name: Web Protocols
techniques.description: Adversaries use HTTP or HTTPS headers and POST bodies to beacon and transmit instructions between agents and C2.

techniques.name: DNS
techniques.description: Adversaries tunnel commands and data inside DNS query responses and TXT records (DNS tunneling).

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Adversaries download additional tools, payloads, or modules from external infrastructure onto compromised systems.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
techniques.description: Adversaries exfiltrate stolen company data directly through the primary command and control connection.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
techniques.description: Adversaries upload stolen data to legitimate cloud storage services (MEGA, Dropbox, Google Drive, AWS S3).

techniques.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
techniques.description: Adversaries encrypt victim data using symmetric/asymmetric algorithms (Ransomware) to extort payments and halt business operations.

techniques.name: Data Destruction
techniques.description: Adversaries destroy data and files on targeted systems to disrupt business functions and prevent incident response.

techniques.name: Service Stop
techniques.description: Adversaries stop or terminate critical operating system and application services (database engines, web servers) to cause downtime.

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information on Mobile
techniques.description: Adversaries compress or encrypt mobile application code to evade app store review and on-device detection.

techniques.name: Location Tracking
techniques.description: Adversaries track victim physical movements by tapping GPS, Wi-Fi BSSID, and cellular cell tower location sensors.

techniques.name: Unauthorized Command Message
techniques.description: Adversaries send unauthorized industrial protocol command messages (Modbus, DNP3, CIP) to alter physical machinery behavior.

techniques.name: Denial of Service in ICS
techniques.description: Adversaries flood safety controllers with packets to blind operators during anomalous physical process conditions.

campaigns.name: SolarWinds Supply Chain Compromise
campaigns.description: Global supply chain intrusion in 2020 compromising Orion software updates to target top-tier organizations.

campaigns.name: Colonial Pipeline Cyberattack
campaigns.description: 2021 DarkSide ransomware attack impacting refined petroleum pipeline operations across the US East Coast.

campaigns.name: U.S. Water Utilities Cyber Intrusions
campaigns.description: Documented in v20: State-sponsored intrusions exploiting internet-exposed Unitronics and PLC controllers in municipal water treatment facilities.

campaigns.name: AI-Assisted Breach of Mexican Government Infrastructure
campaigns.description: Documented in v20: Complex multi-tier intrusion leveraging generative AI prompt injection and credential synthesis across government IT and OT networks.

procedures.description: APT29 duplicated LSASS tokens to escalate privileges on compromised domain controllers and forge cloud SAML tokens.
Cobalt Strike Beacon executes PowerShell commands encoded in Base64 via powershell.exe -NoP -NonI -W Hidden -Enc.
Lazarus Group modified registry keys to disable Windows Defender real-time monitoring and killed EDR processes.
Adversaries used stolen SAML token signing certificates to forge cloud access tokens across Azure AD.
Mimikatz queries LSASS process memory using sekurlsa::logonpasswords to harvest cleartext passwords and NTLM hashes.
DarkSide affiliates used Salsa20 and RSA-1024 encryption routines to lock corporate domain controllers and file servers.
Volt Typhoon exploited zero-day flaws in internet-facing Fortinet and Ivanti VPN appliances to enter US infrastructure.
Scattered Spider launched repeated Push Notification fatigue floods against corporate helpdesks to bypass MFA.
Storm-0501 inputted direct prompt injection payloads into internal IT helpdesk AI chatbots to force the assistant to dump active directory credentials.
Adversaries embedded hidden zero-font prompt injection instructions inside submitted PDF tenders that coerced government LLM review tools to grant elevated access.
CyberAv3ngers flooded industrial MQTT broker topics with forged control messages to force shutdown of municipal water filtration pumps.
Lazarus Group hosted fake cryptocurrency trading Android APKs on third-party sites, instructing victims to bypass OS sideloading protections.

mitigations.name: Privilege Account Management
mitigations.description: Enforce strict separation between standard accounts and administrative accounts with Just-In-Time access.

mitigations.name: Disable or Restrict Feature or Program
mitigations.description: Disable PowerShell v2 and constrain PowerShell language modes to ConstrainedLanguage to prevent script execution.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.description: Ensure EDR agent directory files and security driver registry paths are read-only for system administrators.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.description: Implement firewall egress filtering and block unauthorized outbound ports (e.g. non-standard HTTP/S or direct SMB 445).

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.description: Deploy EDR agents with kernel-mode drivers and enable Windows Credential Guard (LSA Protection).

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.description: Train employees to recognize social engineering tactics, spearphishing attachments, and MFA prompt bombing.

mitigations.name: Prompt Injection Mitigation & Input Sanitization
mitigations.description: Implement strict input sanitization, delimiter escaping, and prompt firewalls to block adversarial injections before reaching LLMs.

mitigations.name: AI Model Output Filtering & Tool Sandboxing
mitigations.description: Verify and enforce strict JSON schemas for LLM tool invocations and enforce human-in-the-loop approvals for sensitive actions.

mitigations.name: Industrial Broker Access Control
mitigations.description: Enforce mTLS authentication and strict ACLs on MQTT and DDS industrial pub/sub brokers.

detections.strategy: Monitor process access and token duplicate API calls targeting lsass.exe (e.g. OpenProcess, DuplicateTokenEx).
analytics: SIGMA: Suspicious Token Duplication via WinAPI

detections.strategy: Monitor service stop requests and registry modifications under HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender.
Enable Script Block Logging (Event ID 4104) and monitor suspicious parameters like -EncodedCommand and -ExecutionPolicy Bypass.
analytics: SIGMA: Obfuscated PowerShell Execution via Command Line

detections.strategy: Detect non-system processes requesting PROCESS_VM_READ access rights to the lsass.exe process handle.
analytics: Sysmon Event ID 10: LSASS Memory Access

detections.strategy: Detect high-volume file modification bursts with mass extension changes across user and network shared volumes.
analytics: SIGMA: Rapid File Extension Modification by Untrusted Binary

detections.strategy: Inspect incoming LLM prompt streams for known adversarial jailbreak patterns, system prompt overrides, and delimiter escaping.
analytics: SIGMA: LLM Direct Prompt Injection Pattern
AI Gateway: Jailbreak Keyword Anomaly Trigger

detections.strategy: Monitor industrial MQTT broker telemetry for unauthorized publish commands targeting critical process actuator topics.
analytics: Zeek: Unauthorized MQTT Publish to Industrial Actuator Topic
OT SIEM: Process Variable Setpoint Anomaly

d3fendTechniques.name: System Process Mapping
d3fendTechniques.description: Constructing verified lineage graphs and parent-child relationship models for all authorized processes on the host.

d3fendTechniques.name: Network Asset Mapping
d3fendTechniques.description: Baselining all corporate endpoints, domain controllers, and cloud VMs to identify rogue network connections.

d3fendTechniques.name: Access Control Verification
d3fendTechniques.description: Verifying authorization tokens, scope boundaries, and cryptographic claims before allowing high-privilege operations.

d3fendTechniques.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
d3fendTechniques.description: Enforcing phishing-resistant hardware FIDO2/WebAuthn credentials across all remote login endpoints.

d3fendTechniques.name: Executable Header Protection
d3fendTechniques.description: Enforcing ASLR, DEP, and Control Flow Guard (CFG) across all user and kernel binary headers.

d3fendTechniques.name: Prompt Injection Firewall
d3fendTechniques.description: Filtering and sanitizing inputs to LLM gateways using semantic boundary checks and delimiter isolation to prevent prompt hijacking.

d3fendTechniques.name: Process Execution Analysis
d3fendTechniques.description: Analyzing command line arguments, child process spawns, and in-memory execution paths for anomalies.

d3fendTechniques.name: Network Traffic Analysis
d3fendTechniques.description: Inspecting packet headers, TLS SNI certificates, and beacon jitter for command and control channels.
d3fendTechniques.ruleSnippet: alert tls where ja3_hash in blacklist_c2_hashes;

d3fendTechniques.name: File Modification Analysis
d3fendTechniques.description: Monitoring filesystem I/O operations for abnormal file encryption rates and bulk extension changes.

d3fendTechniques.name: Model Output Filtering
d3fendTechniques.description: Validating generative AI responses against schema invariants, regex rules, and hallucination detectors before action execution.

d3fendTechniques.name: Software Health Monitoring
d3fendTechniques.description: Monitoring security agent telemetry and isolating endpoints when EDR protection is terminated.

d3fendTechniques.name: Endpoint Isolation & Disconnect
d3fendTechniques.description: Cutting off host network interfaces to contain active lateral movement while preserving SOC forensic tunnel.

d3fendTechniques.name: OT Publish/Subscribe Protocol Whitelisting
d3fendTechniques.description: Segmenting industrial IoT brokers and strictly enforcing topic publish/subscribe authorization lists.

d3fendTechniques.name: Decoy Environment Deployment
d3fendTechniques.description: Deploying realistic high-interaction decoy servers on the corporate subnet to trap scanning adversaries.

d3fendTechniques.name: Honeytoken Seeding
d3fendTechniques.description: Placing fake AWS access keys and decoy Domain Admin credentials into memory and files to detect theft.

d3fendTechniques.name: Token Revocation & Session Eviction
d3fendTechniques.description: Immediately invalidating OAuth refresh tokens, Kerberos TGT tickets, and active logon sessions across Active Directory.

d3fendTechniques.name: Kernel Process Eviction & Termination
d3fendTechniques.description: Terminating malicious threads and processes at the kernel driver layer to bypass userland hook evasion.

d3fendTechniques.name: System Restore & Immutable Snapshot Recovery
d3fendTechniques.description: Restoring operating system state and critical volumes from immutable, write-once cloud or hardware snapshots.

d3fendTechniques.name: Backup Reconstruction & Verification
d3fendTechniques.description: Rebuilding corrupted domain databases and cluster volumes from verified offline air-gapped backups.
